findings.statement: CXCR2 is the top convergence candidate and the only top-ranked gene with all of: strong biopsy upregulation, human genetic support and clinical-stage small-molecule drugs (reparixin Phase 3; navarixin, ladarixin, SX-682, elubrixin, danirixin Phase 2, all in other indications per Open Targets). Open Targets association with UC is [gene=CXCR2; type=open_targets_association; source=Open Targets Platform; score=0.5345], and meta-analysis log2FC is [gene=CXCR2; type=expression_meta; source=DATASET:META; layer=rna; log2fc=2.264]. No UC-specific approved drug; this is a repurposing candidate.

CXCR2 belongs to Reactome pathways Neutrophil degranulation, Chemokine receptors bind chemokines and G alpha (i) signalling events; STRING high-confidence partners are the ELR+ CXC chemokines CXCL8, CXCL1, CXCL5, CXCL2, CXCL6 and CXCL3, which places it in a neutrophil-recruitment axis shared with CXCL8, CXCL1 and CXCL5 in the ranking.

CXCL8 is strongly induced in UC biopsies (meta-analysis log2FC [gene=CXCL8; type=expression_meta; source=DATASET:META; layer=rna; log2fc=3.704]) but has weak genetic support: Open Targets association [gene=CXCL8; type=open_targets_association; source=Open Targets Platform; score=0.1087] and zero genetic component in the convergence ranking. Only antibody-type clinical drugs are listed (ABX-IL8 and adakitug, Phase 2), so the signal is expression-led and likely reflects neutrophil infiltration rather than a causal variant.

JAK2 is a genetically supported gene with a modest change in biopsies: Open Targets association [gene=JAK2; type=open_targets_association; source=Open Targets Platform; score=0.7318] (second among known UC targets) against a meta-analysis log2FC of only [gene=JAK2; type=expression_meta; source=DATASET:META; layer=rna; log2fc=0.872]. It is druggable (fedratinib approved, in another indication), but the genetics-led support is not matched by a large expression change.

OSMR combines genetic support (Open Targets association [gene=OSMR; type=open_targets_association; source=Open Targets Platform; score=0.3907]) with upregulation in all replication streams. Antibody tractability is Advanced Clinical, with vixarelimab (Phase 2) the only drug listed (not a UC indication). Its single Reactome pathway is IL-6-type cytokine receptor ligand interactions.

CHI3L1 has one of the largest expression changes in the top 40 (meta-analysis log2FC [gene=CHI3L1; type=expression_meta; source=DATASET:META; layer=rna; log2fc=4.714]), but no Open Targets genetic association and no drug, so it is a biomarker candidate rather than a drug target.

FCGR2A has strong genetic support (Open Targets association [gene=FCGR2A; type=open_targets_association; source=Open Targets Platform; score=0.5543]) and replicated but small upregulation; no clinical drug is listed, so it is genetics-led and not currently druggable by listed compounds.

IDO1 is strongly upregulated (meta-analysis log2FC [gene=IDO1; type=expression_meta; source=DATASET:META; layer=rna; log2fc=3.445]) with no genetic association (zero genetics component). Linrodostat (Phase 3) and epacadostat are listed, but in other indications; any UC use would be repurposing with no human-genetic backing.

CD274 (PD-L1) is upregulated and genetically associated (Open Targets association [gene=CD274; type=open_targets_association; source=Open Targets Platform; score=0.3919]). Approved PD-L1 blockers exist, but they are checkpoint inhibitors for oncology; the direction of benefit in UC would be agonism or restoration, not blockade, so existing drugs do not map directly.

MMP1 is strongly and consistently upregulated across cohorts with no genetic association; marimastat, doxycycline and rebimastat are listed as clinical or approved compounds in other indications, so it is expression-led with a (broad-spectrum) drug route only.

DUOX2 is among the most robustly upregulated genes (replicated in all cohorts, higher in inflamed than non-inflamed mucosa) but has no genetic support in Open Targets and no drug; tractability is only the lowest tier, so it is a biomarker candidate rather than a target.
AQP9 is strongly induced and replicated, but has no genetic evidence and no drug in Open Targets, so it is expression-only and not druggable by listed compounds.

caveats: Established UC targets (TNF, IL23A, IL12B, ITGA4, ITGB7, JAK1, S1PR1) are among the top Open Targets UC associations but TNF and IL23A are not in the stored convergence ranking, so they are not supported by the biopsy expression streams; I did not inspect the others individually.
Drug lists are Open Targets records in any indication, not UC trial results; no UC efficacy is implied.
Open Targets scores combine many evidence types (literature included); genetic component values come from the ranking record.
Only a subset of the top 40 was profiled with open_targets_target and STRING; pathway and interaction data were retrieved only for CXCR2 and OSMR.
Bulk biopsy expression cannot separate epithelial change from infiltrating neutrophils or monocytes, which likely drives CXCL8, CXCR2, S100A8/9 and LCN2.
